And euery day at the end of Ma{{ls}}{{ls}}e.}}{{sc|The}} beginning {{sup|‖}} vvas the {{sc|Word}}, and the {{sc|Word}} vvas {{sup|‖}} vvith God, and {{sup|‖}} God vvas the {{sc|Word}}. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=2}} This vvas in the beginning vvith God. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=3}} Al things vvere made {{sup|‖}} by him: and vvithout him vvas made {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''`nothing that vvas made''.}}`nothing. That vvhich vvas made', {{verse|chapter=1|verse=4}} in him was life, and the life vvas the light of men: {{verse|chapter=1|verse=5}} and the light {{ls}}hineth in darkene{{ls}}{{ls}}e, and the darkene{{ls}}{{ls}}e did not comprehend it. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=6}} There vvas a man {{ls}}ent from God, vvho{{ls}}e name vvas Iohn. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=7}} This man came for te{{ls}}timonie: to giue te{{ls}}timonie of the light, that al might beleeue through him. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=8}} He vvas not the light, but to giue te{{ls}}timonie of the light. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=9}} It vvas the true light, vvhich lighteneth euery man that commeth into this vvorld. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=10}} He vvas in the vvorld, and the vvorld vvas made by him, and the vvorld knevv him not. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=11}} He came into his ovvne, and his ovvne receiued him not. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=12}} But as many as receiued him, {{sup|‖}} he gaue them povver to be made the {{ls}}onnes of God, to tho{{ls}}e that beleeue in his name. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=13}} VVho, not of bloud, nor of the vvil of fle{{ls}}h, nor of the vvil of man, but of God are borne. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=14}} {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ {{sc|Et verbvm caro factvm est}}.}}∷ {{sc|And {{sup|‖}} the vvord vvas made flesh}}, and dwelt in vs (and vve {{ls}}avv the glorie of him, glorie as it vvere of the only-begotten of the Father) ful of grace and<noinclude>{{continues|veritie.⊣}}</noinclude>
